seoDescription: Lost a family member to someone’s negligence in Michigan? ATLAW explains who can file, what the family recovers, the probate step, and the deadlines. Free consultation.
tagline: Who can bring the claim, who shares in the recovery, how the probate court is involved, and how long the family has.
secondaryKeywords: wrongful death statute of limitations michigan

c.v: When a family member dies because someone else was careless, Michigan law gives the family a path to seek compensation. But the process is not always what families expect. The claim belongs to the estate, not to the grieving spouse or child directly; the recovery is distributed with court approval based on the losses suffered by eligible beneficiaries; and the deadline depends on what caused the death. Families who do not know these rules lose time they do not have.

This page explains how a Michigan wrongful death claim works, step by step, so that you can make decisions with the facts in front of you. We also know that nobody reads a page like this unless something terrible has happened. We are sorry that you are here.

sections.heading: Who can file a wrongful death claim in Michigan

c.v: Michigan’s Wrongful Death Act (MCL 600.2922) allows a claim whenever a death was caused by a wrongful act or negligence that would have supported an injury lawsuit had the person lived.
Only the personal representative of the estate can file it.

Not the spouse, not the children, not the parents, unless one of them is appointed personal representative. If the person left a will naming an executor, that person petitions the probate court for appointment. If there was no will, a family member (usually the spouse or an adult child) petitions. The probate court in the county where the person lived issues “letters of authority,” and the personal representative then has the standing to bring the claim and to hire a lawyer for the estate. ATLAW works closely with a probate team to help families navigate the estate-opening process and the appointment of a personal representative as smoothly and efficiently as possible. A fee applies for probate-related services, which we explain before moving forward.
Who shares in the recovery

is set by the Act (MCL 600.2922(3)): the spouse, children, descendants, parents, grandparents, brothers and sisters, the children of the deceased’s spouse, and anyone named in the will. Within 30 days of filing the lawsuit, the personal representative must notify every one of these people in writing that the claim exists and that they may be entitled to share in it (600.2922(4)).
Unborn children.
Michigan allows a wrongful death claim for the death of an embryo or fetus caused by a wrongful act against the mother (MCL 600.2922a), with exceptions for lawful medical procedures.
The Act lists the damages (MCL 600.2922(6)), and a jury or a settlement allocates them:

sections.heading: How the recovery is divided among family members

c.v: This is the part of a Michigan wrongful death case that surprises families. The money does not simply go to the estate and pass under the will. After a settlement or verdict, the personal representative files a motion in the probate court (or the trial court) proposing how to divide the proceeds among the eligible family members, with notice to each of them. If everyone agrees, the court approves the distribution. If they do not, the court holds a hearing and decides, based on each person’s relationship with the deceased and the loss each suffered (MCL 600.2922(6)). A spouse and minor children ordinarily receive the largest shares; an estranged adult child may receive little. Attorney fees and case costs are approved by the court at the same hearing.

Because the division is decided by a court and not by the personal representative alone, families should talk to a lawyer before any family member signs anything with an insurer. An insurer that settles with one family member has not settled the claim.

sections.heading: Fatal car, truck, and motorcycle crashes: two claims, not one

c.v: In 2024, 350 people were killed in traffic crashes in Wayne, Oakland, Macomb, and Washtenaw counties, and 1,099 statewide (Michigan State Police, 2024 Traffic Crash Facts). When a death is caused by a motor vehicle crash, the family may have both no-fault benefit claims and a wrongful death claim, depending on eligibility and liability.
No-fault survivor’s loss benefits

(MCL 500.3108) are paid by the deceased person’s own auto insurer, or by the insurer that would have paid their PIP benefits, regardless of fault. For three years after the death, dependents receive the economic support the person would have provided, up to the same monthly maximum that applies to wage loss ($7,455 per 30-day period for accidents occurring October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027), plus $20 a day in replacement services. The insurer also pays funeral and burial expenses up to the policy’s limit, which Michigan requires to be at least $1,750 and allows up to $5,000 (MCL 500.3107(1)(a)). Written notice to the insurer within one year is required (MCL 500.3145); the family should not wait for the wrongful death case to resolve before claiming these.
The wrongful death lawsuit

against the at-fault driver is separate, and recovers everything no-fault does not: pain and suffering before death, loss of society and companionship, and economic support beyond the three years and above the monthly cap. In a crash, the injury threshold does not apply to a death; the family may sue for non-economic damages without proving a serious impairment (MCL 500.3135(1)). Comparative fault still applies: if the deceased was more than 50% at fault, non-economic damages are barred.
For a death caused by a
drunk driver

, the bar or store that served the driver while visibly intoxicated may be liable under Michigan’s dram shop act (MCL 436.1801), with written notice to the retailer required within 120 days and a two-year deadline.

faqs.question: Who can file a wrongful death lawsuit in Michigan?

answer.v: Only the personal representative of the estate, appointed by the probate court (MCL 600.2922). A spouse, child, or parent can be appointed, but must be, before the claim can be filed.

The spouse, children, descendants, parents, grandparents, siblings, stepchildren, and anyone named in the will may share. The probate court approves the division after a hearing, based on each person’s relationship and loss.

Three years from the death for most claims; two years (with a six-month Notice of Intent) for medical malpractice; one year to claim no-fault survivor’s loss benefits; 120 days to notify a government body. The savings provision can extend the deadline for an estate in limited circumstances, but should not be relied on.

faqs.question: My family member died in a car accident. What does no-fault pay?

answer.v: Survivor’s loss benefits: up to three years of the economic support the person provided, capped at the monthly maximum, plus $20 a day in replacement services and funeral expenses up to the policy limit. These are separate from, and in addition to, the wrongful death claim against the at-fault driver.

faqs.question: Is there a cap on wrongful death damages in Michigan?

answer.v: No, except in medical malpractice cases, where non-economic damages are capped under MCL 600.1483. Economic damages are never capped.

faqs.question: Can we recover for pain and suffering?

answer.v: Yes, for the pain and suffering the person consciously experienced between the injury and death, and separately for the family’s own loss of society and companionship.

faqs.question: What if there was no will?

answer.v: The probate court appoints a personal representative, usually the spouse or an adult child, under Michigan’s intestacy rules. The wrongful death claim proceeds the same way.

faqs.question: What if my family member was partly at fault?

answer.v: The recovery is reduced by their percentage of fault. If they were more than 50% at fault, the family cannot recover non-economic damages. Economic damages are still recoverable, reduced by the share.

faqs.question: Can we sue if the death happened at work?

answer.v: Not the employer, in most cases; workers’ compensation death benefits apply instead. But the family can sue any third party whose negligence caused the death, and those claims are often the larger recovery.

faqs.question: How much does a wrongful death lawyer cost?

answer.v: Nothing up front. ATLAW works on a contingency fee set in writing before we begin and approved by the court at distribution. The family owes no fee unless there is a recovery.
